paragraphs.text: Agents make drafts, and designers make decisions.
The first screen used to be the hard part. Now it takes a prompt and a minute, and it arrives looking finished, but looking finished is not the same as being right.
The teams with the highest bar don’t stop there. At
, designer Isha Kumar routes only 20–30% of new design work through AI and keeps the rest hands-on.
found nearly six in ten people say design matters more since AI arrived, not less.
So give agents the setup, the repetition, the first pass. Then let a designer grab the work and shape it directly, instead of typing a request to nudge the padding and waiting.
A tool that only works through prompts has automated the wrong half.
Judge the ending, not the draft.
